name: Periodic paralysis with later-onset distal motor neuropathy
aliases: Periodic paralysis with distal motor neuropathy
Late-onset distal motor neuropathy with periodic paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for periodic paralysis with distal motor neuropathy

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of flaccid muscle weakness or paralysis typically triggered by rest after exercise or carbohydrate-rich meals
Electrophysiological evidence of distal motor neuropathy manifesting later in disease course
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with periodic paralysis or distal motor neuropathy
Preservation of sensory nerve function on clinical and electrophysiological testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent episodic muscle weakness plus electrophysiological confirmation of distal motor neuropathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; sensory nerves are typically spared.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Later-onset distal motor neuropathy with distal muscle atrophy
searchTerms: late onset weakness and muscle wasting in hands and feet
distal muscle atrophy with motor loss

common.symptomName: Muscle stiffness or cramping preceding paralysis episodes
searchTerms: muscle stiffness or cramps before paralysis

common.symptomName: Reduced deep tendon reflexes in affected limbs
searchTerms: weak reflexes in arms or legs

common.symptomName: Normal sensory examination despite motor deficits
searchTerms: no sensory loss with muscle weakness
muscle tiredness in hands and feet
easily tired muscles in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Transient muscle pain during paralysis episodes
Mild autonomic symptoms such as sweating abnormalities
searchTerms: slight autonomic symptoms like sweating issues
muscle twitching in hands and feet
shortness of breath from weak breathing muscles
breathing difficulty due to muscle weakness

rare.symptomName: Mild sensory neuropathy in late stages
searchTerms: mild nerve sensation loss late in disease

laboratory: Serum potassium levels may be low, normal, or high during paralysis episodes depending on subtype
imaging: Muscle MRI may show fatty replacement and atrophy in distal muscles in advanced stages
other: Electromyography showing myopathic changes during episodes and neurogenic changes consistent with distal motor neuropathy later

distinguishingFeatures: Episodes triggered by rest or fasting with hyperkalemia during attacks
Lack of distal motor neuropathy development
Chronic distal motor neuropathy without episodic paralysis
Fluctuating muscle weakness without episodic paralysis
Presence of autoantibodies and response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors

references: Orphanet: Periodic paralysis with later-onset distal motor neuropathy, ORPHA:397750
Statland JM, Fontaine B, Hanna MG. Periodic Paralysis. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2018;4:43.
Rosenfeld J, et al. Distal motor neuropathy associated with periodic paralysis: clinical and genetic features. Neurology. 2020.
